title: phase-bj: mechanical close flow: close hook, stack bead, sanity-stack, runs tabs
description:
Repository: randlee/atm-bd-orchestration. Code, worktrees, sprint branches and PRs live there, on its `integrate/phase-bj`; atm-core's `integrate/phase-bj` holds only this plan. The rulings are Rand's of 2026-10-18, anchored as ANC-051..089 in `docs/plans/phase-bj/anchors.md`; the requirement docs are `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` of atm-bd-orchestration PR #342 with the dev, dev-sanity, team-lead and quality-mgr requirement items they amend.

## Goal
Dev work is not complete until sanity verifies it, and the lead does not need to intervene between a dev push and the QA assignment:
- one script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes; it checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead;
- the dev's ATM task stays open until the sanity close hook closes it on PASS; a sanity FAIL is one `sanity-fail.xml.j2` message to the dev on that open task, no finding children, counted in `metadata.sanity_round`, escalated to team-lead once the count exceeds `max_sanity_rounds` (default 5);
- the stack bead `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack` is the ledger and the lock of the phase stack; the sanity side links the layer on PASS under its claim, first PASS wins the top and the other dev gets `rebase-required` without a round counted; a sanity-stack subagent handles one next-top layer per spawn, sequentially, with a lean mode and a lock timeout that never blocks the team and never escalates to a person;
- the pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty onto every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead and validates the projected phase graph before writes;
- `atm-bd console` shows a sanity runs tab and a quality runs tab, newest first, QA run-level verdict and elapsed, the dev's name and icon, and an API_FAILURE kind distinct from a FAIL verdict.

Dev and fix assignment stay the lead's (ANC-060); atm-bd assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task (ANC-061).

## Sprints
| Sprint | Title | Relation | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| bj-1 | close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds | root | - |
| bj-2 | stack bead and sprint-family pour: stack-bead.json.j2, pour metadata, pydantic model per bead kind, validate-plan | root | - |
| bj-3 | sanity-stack subagent and dev-sanity PASS wiring: sequential spawns, lock timeout, lean mode | must_follow | bj-1, bj-2, bj-4 |
| bj-4 | console sanity and quality runs tabs; measured elapsed and dev identity in the sanity ledger | parallel_safe | - |
| bj-5 | skill integrity manifest; install verification and hand-runnable plugin doctor | parallel_safe | - |
design:
## Boundary
One boundary: the `plugins/atm-bd-orchestration` package (skills `atm-bd-orchestration` and `atm-beads`, `agents/`) plus the console app `apps/atm-bd-console` it ships.

## Wave table
Each sprint's owned_paths live on its bead; this table carries only order.

| Wave | Sprint | Layer | pr_target | Depends on | target_boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | bj-1 | 1 | integrate/phase-bj | - | skills/atm-bd-orchestration close hook |
| 1 | bj-2 | 2 | integrate/phase-bj | - | skills/atm-beads plan contract and pour |
| 1 | bj-4 | 3 | integrate/phase-bj | - | apps/atm-bd-console runs tabs and the sanity ledger producers |
| 1 | bj-5 | 4 | integrate/phase-bj | - | package integrity manifest, skill install verification and doctor |
| 2 | bj-3 | 5 | sprint/bj-4-runs-tabs | bj-1, bj-2, bj-4 | agents: sanity-stack and dev-sanity PASS path (integration) |

`pr_target` is a lower bound; every dev rebases onto the stack's current top at dev-complete. Critical path 2 (bj-1, bj-2 or bj-4, then bj-3); width 4; sprint count 5.

## Decisions
- The hook is a script the agent runs as the last step of its template.
- The stack bead is poured with the phase root from a template, never created by hand; `validate-plan` requires it (team-lead 13).
- The sanity side links; the lead never links. The lead owns unstack, sync, rebase, merge and every `stack_failed`, always under the stack bead claim (team-lead 42).
- Nothing is a new process artifact: no class beads, outage beads, holds, refusal citations or checker-defect channel (ANC-084..086); the sanity run table template is retired by the runs tab.
acceptance_criteria:
## Success Criteria
- A sanity PASS through the hook closes the dev's task as the lead and assigns QA as the lead; a sanity FAIL sends one `sanity-fail` message on the dev's open task and creates no bead (ANC-053, ANC-056, ANC-072).
- Two branches cut from the same top that both pass sanity: the first advances the stack bead from empty to singleton against trunk, the second is linked as the hosted top in `layers`; a conflicting second branch gets `rebase-required` and `sanity_round` does not move (ANC-065, ANC-067, ANC-071).
- Every sprint's QA PASS at its head; the stack lands on `integrate/phase-bj` of atm-bd-orchestration; `just lint` and `just test` green there.
- `atm-bd skill` verifies every installed file against the selected release manifest and refuses mismatches with the path list; `atm-hook-doctor.py` reports per-file integrity and aggregate PASS/FAIL from the install-recorded manifest.

title: bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds
description:
## Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Refused and cancelled dev/fix closes stay `atm task close <id> refused` (task-close-hook.md 11); a sanity CANNOT_RUN goes through the hook as a refused close (17). Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 065, 070, 071, 072, 086, 089.

## Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). Every template render is `sc_render.render`, strict, never piped into `jq`; every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. One vars file is the `--vars` of every render along dev -> sanity -> QA (ANC-089), so `task-close-vars.j2` `required_variables` are the union of the `required_variables` of these templates, each named once with its owner: `task-close-vars.j2`, `dev-complete.md.j2`, `fix-complete.md.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2`, `sanity-fail.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`, `qa-template.xml.j2`, `qa-complete.md.j2` (all bj-1). The hook renders no bead template; a bead template a later role passes its vars file to joins the union, read from its front matter at test time. A missing or unknown field is an error before any check (task-close-hook.md 2); `commit`, `pr_number` and `branch` must be non-empty except for a fix with `outcome=not_reproducible`, which carries the cited `file:line` instead. The contract keeps distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead` and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task the current role template closes, and an assignment template renders its explicit destination id. Every field, including qa-template's `policy_path` and `reviewers_round1`, comes from the lead's dispatch vars file; the hook derives none. Every rendered body id equals the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch` with HEAD as its head; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD; and HEAD descends from the current stack top. The stack top has one owner, `stack_top()` in `atm-task-close.py`: it reads `metadata.layers[-1]` (`branch`, `head`) by key name from `bd show <stack bead> --json`, or returns `pr_target` and its head when `layers` is empty; the ancestor check and the `not_reproducible` assignment both call it. bj-2's `StackMetadata` in `bead_schema.py` is the one schema; bj-1 defines no model class and imports nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (task-close-hook.md 7). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair by plain `atm send --template`. ANC-052 overrides task-close-hook.md 8's close-report-assign order. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are `stack_top()`'s, so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` = the fix bead (ANC-053, task-close-hook.md 14). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is at most `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` (dev-sanity 29) before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count exceeds `max_sanity_rounds` (the sixth FAIL by default): the hook reopens nothing (task-close-hook.md 16): the checked bead stays closed and the sanity bead is not reset, so `bd ready` does not list it; the script sends team-lead (ANC-057) `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers, closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL and returns `ok` with `"escalated": "SANITY.ROUND_CAP"`, exit 0; the dev's task stays open until team-lead rules. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (task-close-hook.md 17, dev-sanity 31); the refused close is the only message and no bead is created (ANC-086). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: `verdict` accepts only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`, and only FAIL writes `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057); `tests/test_install.py` covers the render.
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). In the same change `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` drops step e3 (the `sanity-run-table.md.j2` render, a template bj-4 deletes) and step f's reference to it. No template names `--skip-checks`. `dev-complete.md.j2` and `fix-complete.md.j2` describe themselves as the body of the hook's `atm send --template` report, not of `atm task close`; `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`'s FAIL wording says the dev was sent `sanity-fail`, with no filed findings.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`, and its two diagram steps (`docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md`, `docs/diagrams/sprint.md`) redrawn as the hook's `sanity-fail` message to the dev; `docs/requirements/dev-sanity.md` is atm-bd-orchestration PR #342's (its item 47 records the script as retired); `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47). The generated block of `manifest.yaml` is regenerated with `tests/gen_manifest.py` in this layer (it adds the hook, the three templates and the examples and drops the deleted script), never hand-edited. `config/legacy-owned.json` keeps its pre-0.2.3 hashes unchanged.
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing. The stack-bead fixture `scripts/tests/fixtures/stack-bead.json` is a byte copy of bj-2's `stack-bead.json.j2` design example; nonempty-ledger cases append `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` entries to its `layers` in the test.
13. Replay safety, from existing bead metadata and ATM task events, no second ledger: before each write the hook reads bead state and `atm task events`; a write already recorded with the same key is skipped, one recorded with a different verdict or sha is `REPLAY.CONFLICT`. The key is (role task id, verdict, sha); the FAIL counter's key adds the sanity task's current assignment event id, written as `sanity_round_key` in the same `bd update --set-metadata` as `sanity_round`, so a replay never double-counts and two FAILs on two assignments at one head count twice. A replayed assignment is a same-id update (atm-core #1619), never a second task.

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, by key name (deliverable 4).
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

## Public Contract
```
atm-task-close.py --role dev|fix|sanity|qa --vars <file> [--skip-checks]
stdout: {"ok": {"role": ..., "bead": ..., "commit": ..., "pr_number": ..., "github": "ok"|"unavailable", "assigned": [<task ids>], "closed": [<bead ids>]}}
      | {"err": {"code": "VARS.MISSING"|"VARS.EMPTY"|"VARS.UNKNOWN"|"VARS.INVALID"|"HEAD.DIRTY"|"HEAD.NOT_PUSHED"|"BASE.NOT_ANCESTOR"|"PR.NOT_FOUND"|"SANITY.NOT_STACKED"|"BEAD.NO_SANITY"|"REPLAY.CONFLICT", "message": ..., "fix": ...}}
exit 0 on ok, 1 on err
```
GitHub unavailable is `ok` with `"github": "unavailable"`; the round cap is `ok` with `"escalated": "SANITY.ROUND_CAP"` (exit 0). `PR.NOT_FOUND`: no open PR for `branch` whose head is HEAD; the PR base is not checked.

Identity per command (task-close-hook.md 4):
```python
LEAD_ENV = {**os.environ, "ATM_IDENTITY": lead, "ATM_TEAM": team}   # atm task assign; atm task close <checked bead>
run(["atm", "task", "assign", member, "--task-id", bead, "--template", tpl, "--vars", vars_path], env=LEAD_ENV)
run(["bd", "close", bead, "--reason", reason, "--actor", os.environ["ATM_IDENTITY"]])        # caller
```
`task-close-vars.j2` header:
```
---
name: task-close-vars
format: text
required_variables per role per deliverable 2.
---
```
`main(argv, runner=subprocess.run, clock=time.monotonic)`: the subprocess runner and the clock are an injectable seam that `test_task_close.py` uses and that another test module (bj-3's `test_sanity_stack.py`) can drive the same way.

Ancestor check: `stack_top()` reads `metadata.layers[-1]["branch"]` by key from `bd show <stack bead> --json`, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<branch> HEAD`; `origin/<pr_target>` only when `layers` is empty. No model class. The PR check: `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls?head=<o>:<branch>&state=open` filtered to number, base.ref, head.sha.

## Exact Targets
- new `scripts/atm-task-close.py`, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, `scripts/tests/fixtures/stack-bead.json`, `templates/task-close-vars.j2`, `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`, `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`, `examples/task-close-vars-{dev,fix,sanity,qa}.json`
- edited `templates/dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2`, `qa-template.xml.j2` (close steps), `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2`, `install.py`, `skills/atm-beads/scripts/repo_config.py`, `scripts/tests/test_templates.py`, `tests/test_install.py`, the generated block of `manifest.yaml` (by `tests/gen_manifest.py`)
- deleted `scripts/sanity-create-findings` and its tests; edited the sanity FAIL step of `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` and `docs/diagrams/sprint.md`

Also owned: the four completion templates, `assignment-gates.py` and its tests, and tests for the deleted sanity-create-findings script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity.

- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id; the rendered `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` FAIL body names no finding bead.
- [ ] (ANC-057) six distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting reopen the checked bead on the first five and leave `sanity_round` at 6, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the sixth, the sanity bead not reset, the result `ok` with `escalated: SANITY.ROUND_CAP` and exit 0, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to team-lead; replaying the sixth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the third run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-057) `tests/test_install.py`: an install whose registry has no `max_sanity_rounds` renders `max_sanity_rounds: 5` into `.claude/project/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml`, one with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` renders 2, and `repo_config.load()` returns the rendered value.
- [ ] (ANC-071, ANC-086) in `test_task_close.py`, PASS and CANNOT_RUN runs issue no `sanity_round` write; a `verdict` other than PASS, FAIL or CANNOT_RUN fails `VARS.INVALID` before any write; a CANNOT_RUN run leaves the sanity bead open and unassigned, closes the sanity task `refused`, creates no bead and sends no other message.

- [ ] (ANC-089) each `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json` renders strictly through every template that role passes it to; deleting any one variable from it makes the hook exit with `VARS.MISSING` before any check.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward` = the fix bead; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.

- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` and its two tests are absent, no file under `plugins/` or `docs/diagrams/` names the script, and `tests/gen_manifest.py --check` passes on this layer with the hook, the three new templates and the examples listed and the deleted script not listed.
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; the rendered dev and fix bodies contain no `atm task close ... completed` step; `sanity-fail.xml.j2` and `rebase-required.xml.j2` render strictly with their example vars, the latter naming the checked bead, the branch and the recorded top (ANC-065).

## Goal
The stack bead `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack` exists for every phase as the ledger and the lock of its stack, poured with the phase root and required by `validate-plan`; the pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty onto every bead of a sprint family; a pydantic model per bead kind with one validation over every bead of the phase fails the pour on any missing value. Governing text: `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` 1 and 2, `team-lead.md` 13, 43, atm-bd-orchestration #340. Anchors: ANC-067, ANC-078..083.

## Deliverables
1. `templates/stack-bead.json.j2` (skills/atm-beads): one bead per stack, id `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack`, `issue_type` task, child of the phase root, labels `phase-<x>`, `stage:stack`, metadata `trunk` (the root's `integration_branch`), `stack_number` (null until the first link) and `layers` (empty list). `resources/planning.md` lists it beside `plan-root.json.j2` as rendered with the root into the plan JSONL; the lead creates it by importing that plan JSONL, never by a hand-written `bd create` (team-lead 13; this is the lead creation sanity-stack 1 and task-close-hook 20 name).
2. Layer record: each `layers` entry is `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}`; the last entry is the top; `layers` is the only record of layer order (ANC-067). `bead_schema.py` carries the `StackBead` model with `trunk`, `layers` and the entry model; the claim and the compare-and-set release are plain `bd` commands documented in `resources/orchestrating.md` ("Stack bead": `bd update <stack bead> --claim`; release `bd update <stack bead> --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --status open --assignee ""`; the claim's 900 s lease is kept by `bd heartbeat`; an abandoned claim of this stack bead is recovered only with `bd reclaim --id <stack bead> --older-than 1800s`, then `layers` is re-derived from the hosted stack when the ledger disagrees; unscoped `bd reclaim` and event-age-as-lease-expiry are forbidden; ANC-068's claim timeout is the waiting rule, reclaim the abandoned-holder rule), used by sanity-stack (bj-3) and the lead.
3. `validate-plan`: problem 6, the stack bead is missing, is not a child of the root, or its `metadata.trunk` differs from the root's `integration_branch`; `--file` mode accepts the rendered stack bead in the file. Problem 6 applies to a phase whose root is open; a closed root is not checked; the problem line names the fix (render `stack-bead.json.j2` with the root vars and `bd import` it), so an open older phase gains the bead the same way.
4. Pour metadata (#340 item 1): the producers are `formulas/sprint-group.formula.toml.j2` and `formulas/finding-group.formula.toml.j2`; at pour time every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead receives `branch`, `worktree`, `pr_target` and `difficulty`: `bead-groups` copies the sprint container's values onto the sprint group's dev, sanity and qa beads (ANC-078..081). `templates/qa-bead.json.j2` (the QA bead the lead creates for a finding or a quick fix) requires `branch`, `worktree` and `pr_target` from the cut layer it checks and writes all four keys, so it passes the same `stage:qa` model. Beads poured for a blocking finding (the fix group) carry the same four keys from the layer cut (#340 item 2); `assignment-gates.py` is not edited here (its readers already expect the keys on the bead).
5. One model per bead kind (#340 item 3): sprint container, dev, sanity, qa (with `checked_bead` and the round), gate, finding, fix, stack, and the sanity and qa children of a finding or fix; each names its required metadata keys; `extra="allow"` stays. `bead_schema.py validate --phase <x>` walks every bead under the phase epic (`bd list -l phase-<x> -n 0 --json`, never `--all`), picks the model from the `stage:*` label, including `stage:dev` (the root by its id, a gate by `issue_type` gate); a bead with no model is itself a problem (`<bead>: no model`), so the walk skips none (ANC-083); it exits non-zero naming each bead and missing key (#340 item 4). `bead-groups` validates the exact rendered prospective records together with every current phase bead before any persistent attach/write: missing metadata on an existing or prospective bead makes zero mutating calls and leaves the database unchanged; `--validate` uses the same preview path; tests use real sc-compose-rendered records and injected failures. `schemas/*.schema.json` re-exported.
6. `templates/dev-fix.xml.j2` and `examples/dev-fix-vars.json` deleted; `phase-config init` no longer writes `dev_fix` and `validate-plan`/`plan_contract.py` accept a phase file without it (a sanity FAIL reopens the bead in place on the same task; nothing re-assigns a dev after a FAIL: task-close-hook.md 15). Existing phase files that still carry `dev_fix` stay valid: the key is ignored, not existence-checked. Closed sweep, in this layer: `sprint_index_common.py` (`DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` and docstring), `skills/atm-beads/tests/phase_fixtures.py`, `resources/planning.md` and `resources/orchestrating.md`, `skills/atm-bd-orchestration/SKILL.md` (the template-key list, the `test_command`/`lint_command` rows, the sanity-finding routing row, the template table), the `dev-complete.md.j2` description, the dev-fix cases of `test_templates.py`, the `dev_fix` entry in the package `README.md` `[templates]` key list, and the generated manifest/registry blocks re-run by `tests/gen_manifest.py`; `CHANGELOG.md` history and `config/legacy-owned.json` stay.
7. Tests: `bead_schema.py` model per kind with fixtures mirroring live ids (`atm-bi-7`, `atm-bi-7.group-sanity`, `atm-phase-bi.15-sanity`, `atm-phase-bi.18-qa`, a stack bead), the validate walk, `validate-plan` problem 6 and `--file` with the stack bead, `bead-groups` writing the four keys onto dev, sanity and qa beads and failing the pour on a model error.

## Required Work
- The phase-bi live beads are the fixture source: copy their JSON shapes into the tests, do not invent fields.

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- Reading `metadata.layers` in bj-1’s close hook or writing layer updates under the claim in bj-3; this sprint ships the schema, the pour and validation.
- The console dispatch reading the poured keys (atm-core atm-phase-bi.18, phase-bi).

title: bj-3: sanity-stack subagent and dev-sanity PASS wiring: sequential spawns, lock timeout, lean mode
description:
## Goal
On a sanity PASS the sanity side links the checked PR as the new top of the phase stack under the stack bead's claim before the close hook runs; when more than one sanity task is open, or its own inline link failed, dev-sanity spawns the `sanity-stack` subagent, one spawn at a time in verdict order, each handling exactly one next-top layer. The race is the subagent's job: first PASS wins the top, the other dev gets `rebase-required` with no round counted; a lock timeout returns the holder and never blocks the team or escalates to a person. The link commands live in one script, `scripts/sanity-stack-link`, which dev-sanity runs inline and the subagent runs and repairs around, so the race, the lock and lean mode are code under test. This sprint is the top layer (pr_target `sprint/bj-4-runs-tabs`, closure integration): its harness runs the link and bj-1's close hook as landed. Governing text: `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` 1 to 13, `dev-sanity.md` 9, 10, 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, `team-lead.md` 22, 42, 43. Anchors: ANC-065, 066, 067, 068, 069, 071, 084, 086.

## Deliverables
1. `scripts/sanity-stack-link` (new; fixed argv `sanity-stack-link --input <file.json>`, one JSON result on stdout; bd, git, gh and atm through an injectable runner and the clock injectable, as in `atm-task-close.py`): the one owner of the link procedure (sanity-stack.md 2, 4 to 10). Input: `checked_bead`, `branch`, `pr_number`, `commit`, `stack_bead`, `budget` (`full` or `lean`), `timeout_s` (default 60). Claim with `bd update <stack bead> --claim`, retrying every 5 s until `timeout_s` (900 s lease kept by `bd heartbeat`); a claim of THIS stack bead whose lease expired more than 1800 s ago is abandoned and recovered only with `bd reclaim --id <stack bead> --older-than 1800s`, then `layers` is re-derived as below and the result carries `reclaimed` (former holder, claim time); unscoped `bd reclaim` and event age as expiry are never used. A live claim still held at `timeout_s` returns `lock_timeout` (holder, claim time, holder's active task from `atm task list`). Under the lock, in this order with nothing between: re-read `layers` from the bead (never from the input), `git fetch origin`, take the current top branch or `trunk` when the ledger is empty, verify that baseline is an ancestor of `commit`; `full`: link every `linked: false` layer in order then this PR as the new top (`gh stack link <stack_number> <pr>`; the first stack from layers 0 and 1 with `--base <trunk>`), one `/sc-gh-stack-view`; `lean`: the ancestor check is the only divergence check; verify the PR base ref equals the top branch from one filtered REST pull list (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls?state=open&per_page=100 --jq` to number, base, head, sha, draft; never the raw body) and record `linked: false`; append the first empty-ledger PASS as a singleton with base trunk; append the layer; write the metadata with `bd update --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --metadata @file.json` (the commit point); release with `bd update <stack bead> --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --status open --assignee ""`. Results: `stacked` (new top, nullable `stack_number` for an initial singleton), `rebase_required`, `lock_timeout` or `stack_failed`, each with evidence. GraphQL unavailable is detected and forces `lean`; a lean run makes no GraphQL call (ANC-069). Ancestor check fails: `rebase_required`, link nothing, write nothing (ANC-065). Reconcile under the lock, before anything else, when the bead and the hosted chain disagree (a torn link, a reclaimed claim): preserve every `linked: false` entry, mark only proven links linked, record hosted-only results only when uniquely attributable; ambiguity, conflicting ancestry, a failed link, or exit 13 on any `--if-assignee` write returns `stack_failed` with the lock released (when held) and the ledger unchanged.
2. `agents/sanity-stack.md`: a subagent of dev-sanity (tools Bash, Read), one next-top layer per spawn, input the same fenced JSON object. It runs `sanity-stack-link`; on `stack_failed` for a stack reason (stale local tracking, a stack number minted anew, a PR retargeted or closed, a non-linear stack) it claims the stack bead with the same timeout, repairs with the `sc-gh-stack` recipes within this one layer, never rewriting a layer with children, releases, and runs the script once more. It returns the script's result unchanged as one fenced JSON object; unrecoverable stays `stack_failed`, lock released, ledger unchanged. It makes no `atm` write, never refuses the task, never sends the dev a FAIL, never escalates to a person (ANC-068).
3. `agents/dev-sanity.md` PASS and FAIL paths (dev-sanity 13, 28, 29, 32; sanity-stack.md 11 to 13): one sanity task open: dev-sanity runs `sanity-stack-link` itself; more than one open, or its inline run returned `stack_failed`: it spawns `sanity-stack`, one spawn at a time in verdict order, never two in flight, waiting for each result before the next, so no second writer of the same identity exists (ANC-066). `stacked`: run `atm-task-close.py --role sanity` with the stack result in the vars. A `not_reproducible` fix has no new PR: dev-sanity verifies the cited `file:line` at the commit and branch the assignment names (the current stack top as bj-1 deliverable 4 defines it), runs no link, and closes PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result, which bj-1 deliverable 6 accepts. `rebase_required`, and a pre-claim `sanity-split` `COMMIT_MISMATCH` (dev-sanity 13): reopen the checked bead to the dev, send `rebase-required.xml.j2` on the dev's open task, leave `sanity_round` unchanged, keep the PASS in the ledger, close nothing (ANC-071). `lock_timeout`: keep the sanity task active, send the holder one plain message asking for the release, continue other sanity checks, re-spawn after the holder's reply or after another `timeout_s`; never refuse, never FAIL the dev, never a person (ANC-068). A result carrying `reclaimed` is told to the lead in one plain message. `stack_failed` from the subagent: dev-sanity reports it to the lead as stack owner with the evidence and keeps the task active until the lead says to re-run the link (team-lead 22). FAIL: the close hook with verdict FAIL and the selected undone deliverables with their reasons; the round counter and the cap are the hook's (bj-1 deliverable 6, task-close-hook.md 16); the `sanity-create-findings` FAIL text is removed. The "after a dev-fix" wording (bj-2 deletes `dev-fix.xml.j2`) becomes "after a sanity FAIL reopened the bead" (task-close-hook.md 15). `budget` is `lean` when GraphQL is unavailable or the agent is watching its token budget.
4. `agents/dev-sanity.md` items 9 and 10 (ANC-084, ANC-086): one Jev client call per JEV slot; Jev retries, an API-busy answer retried up to three times, belong to bj-4's `jev_client.py`; an `sc-sanity-llm` spawn that fails with an API error is re-spawned up to three times before that slot reports failure (dev-sanity 9). The failure reason is the verbatim error, kept in the run's ledger row (bj-4's row fields) as kind `API_FAILURE`, never a FAIL verdict; every fallback use is logged with its verbatim error and said once in the close report. The LLM spawn is fenced by a start and end timer whose elapsed is written as `llm_elapsed_s` to the ledger row. The Mandatory Console Report section and its `sanity-run-table.md.j2` render are removed (bj-4 deletes the template; its Sanity tab replaces the table). No class bead, outage bead, hold on re-dispatch, refusal citation or checker-defect side channel appears anywhere in the agent text.
5. `manifest.yaml` ships `agents/sanity-stack.md` and `scripts/sanity-stack-link`; the generated block is regenerated with `tests/gen_manifest.py` in this layer and again after rebase, never hand-merged; `install.py` copies them like the other agents and scripts without a code change.
6. `CHANGELOG.md`: the phase entry for bj-1 to bj-5, written here because this sprint is the top layer.
7. Tests: `scripts/tests/test_agent_prompts.py`, the phrase test of the two prompts (deliverables 2 to 4); `scripts/tests/test_sanity_stack.py`, the scratch end-to-end harness this sprint owns: a scratch git repository with an `origin`, one in-memory bd/gh/atm state behind the injected runner, a controlled clock, driving `sanity-stack-link` and then bj-1's `atm-task-close.py --role sanity` as landed. No live bd, gh, GitHub or ATM, no sleeps.

## Required Work
- Prompt text is minimal: a procedure, not an essay; the link procedure is stated once, in the script.

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- The lead's stack recipes (unstack, restack, land under the claim): the `sc-gh-stack` skill and `team-lead.md` 42 already state them; no script is added for them.

## Recovery and Retry
Recovery is `sanity-stack-link` code driven in `test_sanity_stack.py` by injected clock and runner responses: scoped reclaim of an abandoned claim, re-derived `layers`, preserved ledger-only unlinked lean entries, uniquely attributable hosted links only, fail closed on ambiguity and on exit 13.

## Public Contract
`sanity-stack-link --input <file.json>`; the same object is the `sanity-stack` subagent's fenced input, and the script's stdout is its fenced result:
```json
{"checked_bead": "atm-bj-1", "branch": "sprint/bj-1-task-close-hook", "pr_number": 351, "commit": "<sha>",
 "stack_bead": "atm-phase-bj.stack", "budget": "full", "timeout_s": 60}
```
```json
{"result": "stacked", "top": {"branch": "...", "pr": 351, "head": "<sha>", "base": "...", "linked": true}, "stack_number": 7, "reclaimed": null}
{"result": "rebase_required", "top": {"branch": "...", "head": "<sha>"}, "evidence": "origin/<top> is not an ancestor of <sha>"}
{"result": "lock_timeout", "holder": "<identity>", "claimed_at": "<iso>", "holder_task": "<task id or null>"}
{"result": "stack_failed", "evidence": "<command> [<exit>] <first stderr line>"}
```
Lock, under which the whole procedure runs:
```bash
bd update "$STACK" --claim --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"                       # retry every 5 s until timeout_s; 900 s lease kept by bd heartbeat
bd reclaim --id "$STACK" --older-than 1800s --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"      # abandoned claim of this stack bead only; never unscoped
bd update "$STACK" --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --metadata @layers.json --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"   # the commit point; exit 13 on mismatch
bd update "$STACK" --if-assignee "$ATM_IDENTITY" --status open --assignee "" --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"   # release; exit 13 on mismatch
```
Lean verification (no GraphQL):
```bash
gh api "repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls?state=open&per_page=100" --jq '.[] | {number, base: .base.ref, head: .head.ref, sha: .head.sha, draft}'
```

## Exact Targets
- new `plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/agents/sanity-stack.md`, `skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/sanity-stack-link`, `scripts/tests/test_agent_prompts.py`, `scripts/tests/test_sanity_stack.py`
- edited `plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/agents/dev-sanity.md`, `manifest.yaml` (generated block), `CHANGELOG.md`

This is the top layer: `pr_target` `sprint/bj-4-runs-tabs`, which contains bj-1, bj-2 and bj-4 once rebased; the dev rebases onto the stack's current top at dev-complete and re-runs `gen_manifest.py`.

title: bj-5: skill integrity manifest; install verification and hand-runnable doctor
description:
## Goal
For atm-bd-orchestration issue #349: atm-bd's built wheel and sdist carry a manifest of every shipped skill file's sc-sha; `atm-bd skill` verifies the files it installs against that published manifest; a hand-runnable plugin doctor checks an installed copy without atm-core. The manifest detects skill files that differ from what was published (a tag clone, a bundled tree or an installed copy changed after release); it is not a signature and does not defend a tampered artifact. This is phase-bj work in atm-bd-orchestration, independent of bj-1 through bj-4. Anchors: ANC-087, ANC-088, ANC-003, ANC-010, ANC-011, ANC-012. No SHA is written into any source file; hashing is the `sc-sha` package's `sc_sha` module; the sc-publish kit (`.github/scripts`, `.github/actions`) is unchanged.

## Deliverables
1. `apps/atm-bd-console/hatch_build.py`: in `_include_skills`, after choosing the bundled skill tree, write `skill-manifest.json` (schema version, atm-bd version, one `{path, sc_sha}` per shipped file in sorted path order, where the shipped set is every file of the bundled skill tree except `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` (installers byte-compile into the package), and `sc_sha.calculate_composition_hash` over them) into the build output and force-include it beside the bundled skills in both the wheel and the sdist. This is the published manifest: it exists only in the built artifacts that sc-publish uploads, never in git.
2. `apps/atm-bd-console/pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`: add `sc-sha>=1.7.0,<2` to the runtime dependencies and to the build-system requires, so `import sc_sha` works in the build and in an installed atm-bd. `sc_sha.calculate_hash` is the per-file hash; no other hasher is written.

Sources of the published manifest: bare `atm-bd skill` reads the one packaged in the installed wheel (no network, ANC-010); `atm-bd skill x.y.z` reads it from the `atm_bd-<x.y.z>.tar.gz` asset of the repository's `v<x.y.z>` GitHub release, and `--latest` reads it from the same asset of the repository's latest published release (`releases/latest`, tag `v<version>`), whose tag it installs (ANC-012). 4. `apps/atm-bd-console/src/atm_bd_console/skill_source.py`: `--latest` resolves the repository's latest published release and clones its `v<version>` tag instead of `main`; bare keeps the packaged files (ANC-010) and `x.y.z` keeps cloning the `vX.Y.Z` tag of atm-bd-orchestration (ANC-011).

After `installer.apply_plan`, call `write_install_record` with the version, commit and the sc-sha of each file as installed (rendered team, prefix and member values make installed bytes differ from published bytes by design). The `installed ... from <ref> @ <commit> (atm-bd <version>)` line is unchanged (ANC-003); the `--latest` help reads `install the latest published release`. design:
## Public Contract
Published manifest: `skill-manifest.json` inside the atm-bd wheel and sdist, written by the build hook at build time: `{schema: 1, version, files: [{path, sc_sha}], aggregate}`. Paths are relative to the plugin root and sorted; `aggregate` is `sc_sha.calculate_composition_hash` over the sorted list.

`atm-bd skill` (bare, `x.y.z`, `--latest`) verifies every file of the resolved tree against the manifest of the release it installs before calling the installer; mismatch = exit 1, one `modified|missing|extra <path>` line each, nothing written; a release without a published manifest is refused the same way. Install record `<dest>/atm-bd-install.json`: `{version, commit, source, files: [{path, sc_sha}]}` with installed-file hashes.

`atm-hook-doctor.py [--dest <dir>]`: per-path `ok|modified|missing|extra`, aggregate `PASS|FAIL`, exit 0/1; `atm-hook-doctor.py doctor` reads `{"schema_version","hook":"doctor","team","phase","custom"}` on stdin and prints `doctor(request: dict) -> dict` = `{"success": bool, "message": str, "findings": [{"severity": "info|warning|error", "code": str, "message": str, "remediation": str|null}]}` (atm-core #1877, ADR-068 D6).

vertical_rationale: the build hook writes the manifest, `atm-bd skill` verifies against it and writes the install record, and the plugin doctor reads that record, so the console app and the plugin script share one manifest and record format and close together.

See owned_paths. `install.py`, `.github/**` and every bj-1..bj-4 file are untouched.
